papers.title_in_file: Optimization by Quantum Annealing: Lessons from hard 3-SAT cases
papers.version_note: arXiv:cond-mat/0502468v1, 18 Feb 2005; matches the record. The 1x1 inline stencil images pdfimages lists are not figures.
sections_read: III. THE PATH-INTEGRAL MONTE CARLO SCHEME
IV. NUMERICAL EXPERIMENTS: COMPARING CLASSICAL AND QUANTUM ANNEALING
V. MONTE CARLO TIME DYNAMICS AND EVOLUTIONARY ANALOGY
VI. AUTOCORRELATION ANALYSIS AND LANDSCAPE PROBING

figures.shows: Residual energy (y, log scale, about 10 to 100) against total annealing time (x, log scale, 100 to 1e+06) for CA, PIMC-QA (P=50), PIMC-QA + G (P=50), Field Cycling and a dashed Gardner Energy line at about 7. CA ends lowest, PIMC-QA + G above it, PIMC-QA highest; the field-cycling points lie below CA at short times and merge with CA near 1e+05. Inset: final average energy after 2000 QA iterations (y, about 30 to 46) against P (x, 10 to 1000), falling from about 46 at P about 10 to a plateau of about 38 at P of about 100 and above, with a dashed CA line at about 32.
figures.confirmed_by: It can be seen that the linear-schedule CA always performs better than the linear-schedule QA

figures.shows: Configuration energy (y, log scale, label 100) against simulation time (x, 0 to 20000) for PIMC-QA + G double-bracket E, PIMC-QA + G single-bracket E, PIMC-QA double-bracket E, PIMC-QA single-bracket E and CA single-bracket E. All curves drop sharply at the start (QUENCHING). The CA curve then falls well below the four QA curves, flattening near 20000. The QA curves decline more slowly and flatten near about 17000 to 20000 (TARGET SELECTION). Inset: coupling JΓ (y, log, about 0.1 to 10) against Γ (x, 0.001 to 1), decreasing as Γ increases.
figures.confirmed_by: Three diﬀerent regimes can be distinguished, which will be called quenching, search (driven by quantum ﬂuctuations) and target selection.

figures.shows: Overlap between configurations K(t*, τ) (y, 0.7 to 1) against autocorrelation time τ (x, 0 to 100) for CA, one curve per fixed simulation time t* from 200 to 2000. Lower curves decay smoothly, the lowest to about 0.72 at τ = 100. Upper curves oscillate regularly and bunch near about 0.9.
figures.confirmed_by: In the ﬁnal part of the classical relaxation, about 20% of the variables are still allowed to ﬂip at each iteration

figures.shows: Overlap between configurations K(t*, τ) (y, 0.7 to 1) against autocorrelation time τ (x, 0 to 100) for QA without global moves (solid) and with global moves (dashed), one curve per t* from 200 to 2000. Lower curves decay like the CA curves of Figure 3. The top solid curve decays slowly from 1 to about 0.93 at τ = 100. The upper dashed curves oscillate and damp near about 0.9 to 0.93.
figures.confirmed_by: If only local moves are performed (solid curves in Fig. 4), no trace of asymptotic periodic behavior is found

figures.shows: Three stacked panels against visited energy (x, 0 to 350): fraction of downhill directions (y, 0 to 0.014), fraction of flat directions (y, 0.09 to 0.16) and fraction of uphill directions (y, 0.83 to 0.91), each with a classical (dashed) and a quantum (solid) average curve over a cloud of sampled points. At the same energy the quantum curve is above the classical one for downhill and flat fractions and below it for uphill. Downhill fraction is about 0 near energy about 40 and rises to about 0.011 (quantum) and about 0.010 (classical) near energy about 350. Flat fraction ends near about 0.147 (quantum) and about 0.143 (classical). Uphill fraction ends near about 0.843 (quantum) and about 0.847 (classical).
figures.confirmed_by: the fractions of downhill, ﬂat and uphill directions are plotted (from top to bottom) against the energy of the visited conﬁgurations.

figures.shows: Three stacked panels against simulation time (x, log, 100 to about 3500). Top: temperature T (y, 0 to 0.35) in steps from about 0.3 down to about 0.05. Middle: quantum coupling JΓ (y, log, 0.001 to 10) as a repeated saw-tooth, rising over each ramp and dropping at the start of the next, about six ramps. Bottom: residual energy (y, log, label 100) for hybrid double-bracket E, hybrid single-bracket E, CA double-bracket E and CA single-bracket E; the hybrid curves fall in steps, one per ramp, with arrows marking quenching levels at T = 0.3, 0.2 and 0.1; the hybrid curves end at or just below the two horizontal CA lines.
figures.confirmed_by: cycling scheme with a total length of 3100 MC iterations

papers.what_it_is: A 2005 numerical study that compares Path-Integral Monte Carlo simulated quantum annealing with classical simulated annealing on one hard random 3-SAT instance with N = 10000 and introduces a field-cycling hybrid schedule.

assertions.value: The authors report that their numerical experiments use a single random 3-SAT instance with N = 10000 variables and clause ratio α = 4.24, right at the border of the SAT/UNSAT transition.
quotes: performed over a single 3-SAT random instance with N = 104 and α = 4.24, (i.e., right at the border
optimization of a large hard instance of the Random 3-SAT Problem (N = 10000)
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own experimental setup in the abstract and in Section IV.
assertions.reader_inference: The text layer prints N = 10 to the fourth as 104; the abstract gives 10000.

assertions.value: The authors state that, using the WalkSAT heuristic supplemented by a message-passing procedure, they verified that the chosen formula at α = 4.24 was satisfiable.
quotes: we veriﬁed that the chosen formula (at α = 4.24) was actually satisﬁable, as expected from theory for α < αc.
the WalkSAT heuristic supplemented by a message-passing procedure
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states a property of its own test instance in its setup.

assertions.value: The paper assigns each clause an energy of 0 if the clause is satisfied and 1 otherwise, and gives the Hamiltonian as the sum over clauses, so that it counts the number of violated clauses.

which simply counts the number of violated clauses.

minimizes the number of violated clauses.

assertions.value: The authors state, citing statistical mechanics work, that the main parameter in the phase diagram of this problem, which determines the hardness of a formula, is the ratio α = M/N of the number M of clauses to the number N of variables.
